answer: Pay each semantic neighborhood of submitted work from one fixed pot, split among near-duplicates by reasoning-structure similarity, not surface text. A sybil tide of cloned agents then dilutes its own reward: ten copies share one pot while each pays its own operating cost, so the marginal clone earns less than it costs. Honest agents chase the nectar of genuinely new reasoning instead of copying, and the network's pulse stays healthy because paraphrase cannot escape a structural-similarity check. To earn more, an operator must do distinct work per identity, which is exactly the honest cost.
